figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of jina-reranker-v3.5. (a) LBNL listwise encoding with a 3L2G hybrid backbone and pinned terminal global layer (G*). (b) Three-stage self-distillation from a full-attention teacher to a sparse-attention student.

Table 1: Overall reranking performance (nDCG@10, %). BEIR, MIRACL, and RTEB use top-100 candidates from jina-embeddings-v5-text-small. Struct-IR† uses the controlled-pool protocol (Table 3). ‡ The RTEB score excludes the MIRACL average score. Best per column in bold, secondbest underlined (first-stage excluded).
Table 7: Multilingual reranking on MIRACL (nDCG@10, %). Columns are models; rows are languages.
Table 9: Representative hyperparameters by training stage.
Table 2: Per-task RTEB results (nDCG@10, %). Columns are models; rows are datasets grouped by domain. Medical CURE reports CUREv1 AVG/en/es/fr.

Figure 2: Constraint-heavy synthetic data for Struct-IR. Left: (i) constraints→query, (ii) perturb hard negative, (iii) dense-mine, (iv) LLM-judge with a promote/refine/discard feedback loop. Right: near-duplicate positive vs. hard negative differing by one field.
Table 6: Reranking performance (nDCG@10, %) on BEIR with top-100 jina-embeddings-v5-text-small candidates. Columns are models; rows are datasets.

Table 4: STARK under the official protocol (Hit@1 / Hit@5 / MRR, %). Entity attributes are rendered as natural-language prose with relational context; top-100 candidates from jina-embeddings-v5-text-small.

Table 5: Inference efficiency on NVIDIA A100 (batch size 1, top-100 listwise reranking, FlashAttention-2). NQ is short-context; AILACasedocs is long-context legal text. Speedup is mean latency of jina-reranker-v3 divided by that of jina-reranker-v3.5.
